parent_v2_1.residual_audit: Most truths remain A/B/M ambiguous after complete presence/absence plus occupied-node arrival times.

question: Which direct mechanism-specific evidence is required to resolve residual BAM decomposition ambiguity?

direct_evidence_definitions.A_direct: Complete idealized abiotic-permissibility state: candidate A mask must equal truth A mask.
direct_evidence_definitions.B_direct: Complete idealized biotic-permissibility state: candidate B mask must equal truth B mask.
direct_evidence_definitions.M_direct: Complete idealized movement state: candidate M mask and full first-arrival vector must equal truth M state.
direct_evidence_definitions.note: These are mechanistic identifiability upper bounds, not realistic field-data claims.

baseline_evidence: positive + perfect negative + occupied-node temporal arrival from v2.1

hypotheses.claim: Adding a direct axis state eliminates exactly those baseline-compatible worlds whose declared state on that axis differs from truth.
hypotheses.rule: Any mismatch between exact axis-state equality and compatibility refutes D1.

hypotheses.claim: Even complete direct A/B/M state evidence cannot distinguish candidate worlds that induce exactly the same A mask, B mask, M mask and full arrival vector.
hypotheses.rule: A unique claim inside a duplicate complete-state equivalence class refutes D2.

hypotheses.claim: A truth world is uniquely identified by complete direct A/B/M state evidence if and only if its complete BAM state tuple is unique in the candidate universe.
hypotheses.rule: Any disagreement between state-tuple uniqueness and final identification refutes D3.

claim_boundary: Direct axis evidence is idealized and used only to diagnose identifiability limits.
Do not interpret complete A/B/M state maps as routinely observable ecological data.
Do not infer parameter values uniquely when multiple parameterizations induce the same state tuple.
